builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: RouteDRAG: Learning to Route and Control Agentic Execution for Multimodal Document RAG
summary: Replaces uniform agentic execution (or fixed short-path RAG) for multimodal document QA with a learned router that predicts per-query whether agent execution helps, plus controlled tool use and termination trained via sequential policy learning. Costs include building a graph-backed multimodal index, training two learned components (operation control, then path routing) on observed outcomes, and maintaining an evolving agent workspace at inference. Can fail if the router miscalibrates on out-of-distribution queries, if training data for policy learning does not reflect production document mix, or if the added pipeline complexity outweighs the modest accuracy gain on simpler workloads.
rationale: The method is implementable on constrained infrastructure since it trains small routing/control policies on top of existing LLM APIs rather than foundation models, but its benefit is workload-dependent and requires the reader to collect outcome data and validate that their query distribution actually contains agent-worthy cases.
technique: Learned routing and control for agentic document RAG

claims.statement: Replaces uniform agentic execution (or fixed short-path RAG) for multimodal document QA with a learned router that predicts per-query whether agent execution helps, plus controlled tool use and termination trained via sequential policy learning. Costs include building a graph-backed multimodal index, training two learned components (operation control, then path routing) on observed outcomes, and maintaining an evolving agent workspace at inference. Can fail if the router miscalibrates on out-of-distribution queries, if training data for policy learning does not reflect production document mix, or if the added pipeline complexity outweighs the modest accuracy gain on simpler workloads.

Average accuracy improvement of 3.47 percentage points over shorter-path-only execution while routing only 79.3% of queries to the agent; also surpasses uniform agent execution with fewer answering calls.
